content: It is a rough road that leads to the heights of greatness.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?
